title: SGB redeemed prematurely by RBI after the 5th year (Aug-2025, before 1-Apr-2026): still exempt under s.47(viic); coupon is not a capital-gains event
covers: interest event ignored for capital gains
rules: Income-tax Act 1961 s.47(viic) (inserted by Finance Act 2016 w.e.f. AY 2017-18): 'any redemption of Sovereign Gold Bond issued by the Reserve Bank of India under the Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, 2015, by an individual' is not a transfer. The clause is not limited to redemption on maturity

Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme 2015 (and each tranche's Government of India notification): early encashment is allowed after the 5th year on coupon dates and is effected by RBI as a redemption of the bond (premature redemption), so it is a 'redemption' within s.47(viic), unlike a sale on the exchange (contrast g10)
Coupon interest (2.5 % p.a.) is income from other sources (s.56), not a capital-gains event; it does not change the lot
Transfer on 12-Aug-2025 is before 1-Apr-2026 -> Income-tax Act 1961 governs; the Finance Act 2026 / Income-tax Act 2025 position (g28) does not apply
derivation: Subscription 2018-02-12 at original issue: 20 units @ 3,000.00 -> cost 60,000.00 (no STT, no charges).
Interest 2024-08-12 of 750.00: income from other sources; ignored for capital gains; lot unchanged.
Premature redemption by RBI 2025-08-12 (held_to_maturity false): 20 @ 9,500.00 -> proceeds 1,90,000.00.
s.47(viic) covers 'any redemption' by an individual, including RBI premature redemption under the Scheme -> not a transfer: gain 0.00, term exempt, rate null.
No taxable capital gains -> exemption_used 0.00, tax 0.00, cess 0.00, total 0.00; no losses.
